notes:
User is a serious/professional photographer and travel enthusiast with a Canon EOS 80D, now taken on five trips (including prior trips to Yellowstone, Yosemite, and Grand Canyon); more trips planned, including Zion National Park. They value sturdy, reliable, precise equipment for landscapes and are considering the Really Right Stuff TVC-34L (or possibly TVC-44L). Advice should assess exact load capacity, required center-of-inverse-mass, ball head, folded dimensions, carry weight, price/value, and whether it meets their actual needs; do not imply a new model or 80D-specific RRS plate without verification.

For Zion and other bright, high-contrast landscape locations, discuss shooting RAW, exposure bracketing/HDR, metering/highlight protection, CPL/GND filters, and using a tripod. The user is investing in Lee Filters’ square filter system and plans to start with a soft graduated ND. Hard grads suit distinct, level horizons; soft grads suit uneven/complex terrain. Lee’s compact Soft Starter Kit (holder, 67 mm ring, 2-stop soft grad, and basics) is a relevant starter choice, but exact compatibility must use the kit lens’s verified thread diameter—likely Canon EF-S 18–135mm f/3.5–5.6 IS USM at 67 mm, but verify rather than assume. Explain holder/ring fit, vignetting, exposure guidance, and mounting practice.

User recently bought a new Lowepro backpack-style camera bag and is happy with it. Do not casually recommend replacing it with the ProTactic 450 AW or another bag; if gear organization becomes an issue, suggest complementary Lowepro pouches, dividers, camera inserts, or accessories. New camera strap also needs adequate attachment/carry considerations. They asked about a bag that fits everything, but current notes already establish satisfaction with their recent Lowepro purchase.

For photo storage, they chose Adobe Creative Cloud’s 1TB plan for professional work because they already use Lightroom and Photoshop and need extensive storage/editing tools. They will keep using Google Photos personally and may explore Adobe Bridge, Camera Raw, or Premiere Pro.

They need a replacement front/rear lens cap for their 18–135mm kit lens. Recommend checking the barrel/camera documentation for exact filter diameter and whether the missing item is front or rear, then buying
trajectory:
User is a serious/professional photographer and travel enthusiast who has taken a Canon EOS 80D on three trips to Yellowstone, Yosemite, and the Grand Canyon, with more trips planned. They are considering a sturdy, reliable tripod, especially the Really Right Stuff TVC-34L, and asked about compatibility. They are also planning to replace a lost/damaged lens cap for their 18–135mm kit lens and want guidance on finding one that fits properly. Likely lens model is Canon EF-S 18–135mm f/3.5–5.6 IS USM, but the exact filter-thread diameter should be verified before recommending a size (often 67 mm, but do not assume).

For photo storage, user decided to use Adobe Creative Cloud’s 1TB plan for professional work because they already use and like Lightroom and Photoshop and need substantial storage/editing tools. They will continue using Google Photos for personal shots. They may also be interested in Adobe Bridge, Camera Raw, or Premiere Pro.

User recently bought a Lowepro backpack-style camera bag and is happy with it. If discussing other bags or organization, acknowledge this and consider complementary Lowepro accessories rather than immediately suggesting a replacement. Relevant camera-bag criteria include protection, capacity, comfort, weather resistance, organization, and accessibility; alternatives previously mentioned included Think Tank, Peak Design, F-Stop, MindShift, and Shimoda.

For the lens cap, recommend checking the lens barrel or camera documentation for the exact filter diameter and thread type, then buying a genuine Canon cap or a reputable third-party cap with a secure fit. Advise checking seller quality/reviews and considering a tether/leash, but avoid treating the assistant’s earlier claim that a Canon 80D-specific RRS camera plate exists as established fact—compatibility should be checked with RRS or an authorized dealer.
